questions.question: During the basic vehicle control skills test:

options.text: A pull-up always counts against the applicant.
A pull-up should be completed at least once.
Stopping without changing direction is not considered a pull-up.
Excessive pull-ups are acceptable in the opinions of some test administrators.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stopping without changing direction is not considered a pull-up.
questions.explanation: A pull-up happens when you stop and pull forward to get a better position. Stopping without changing direction is not a pull-up. Many pull-ups will count as errors.

questions.question: Rust around wheel nuts may mean:

options.text: It recently rained.
The nuts are loose.
The tires should be replaced.
The nuts are too tight.

questions.correctAnswerText: The nuts are loose.
questions.explanation: Rust around wheel nuts usually means they are loose. If you see rust in this area, check if the nuts are tight.

questions.question: When stopping at a railroad crossing, opening the forward door:

options.text: Can help you hear an approaching train.
Should never be done.
May let other noises in, making it harder to hear a train.
Takes too long and is discouraged.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can help you hear an approaching train.
questions.explanation: At a railroad crossing, you can open the forward door if it helps you see or hear an approaching train.

questions.question: Your vehicle's final position should be:

options.text: Exactly where the examiner instructed.
Within five feet of the final position the examiner described.
Wherever you can safely park.
Within two feet of the final position the examiner described.

questions.correctAnswerText: Exactly where the examiner instructed.
questions.explanation: You must park your vehicle in the exact position the examiner described. Not following instructions exactly can result in failing the basic control skills test.

questions.question: When taking the on-road test, you will be evaluated on traffic checks. You should not:

options.text: Scan the road for pedestrians.
Check traffic regularly.
Skip checking your mirrors near intersections.
Check your mirrors regularly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Skip checking your mirrors near intersections.
questions.explanation: During the on-road test, check traffic and your mirrors regularly, especially at intersections. Always scan for pedestrians where they may be present.

questions.question: Eating while driving:

options.text: Saves time.
Is recommended on long trips.
Takes your attention away from driving.
Must be done so cargo stays supervised.

questions.correctAnswerText: Takes your attention away from driving.
questions.explanation: Avoid eating, drinking, or smoking while driving. Anything that takes your focus away from driving is a distraction.

questions.question: Bridges usually:

options.text: Freeze only when the temperature drops well below 32 degrees Fahrenheit.
Freeze after other road surfaces.
Freeze before other road surfaces.
Have heaters to prevent freezing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Freeze before other road surfaces.
questions.explanation: Bridges freeze before the rest of the road. Be extra careful crossing bridges when the temperature is near freezing.

questions.question: If there are no warning gates or lights at a railroad crossing, you should:

options.text: Not worry because the tracks are probably abandoned.
Park and walk to the tracks to check for trains.
Look both ways down the tracks to make sure no trains are coming.
Do what other vehicles around you are doing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look both ways down the tracks to make sure no trains are coming.
questions.explanation: A passive railroad crossing has no gates or warning lights. Before crossing, look down the tracks in both directions for approaching trains.

questions.question: Buses must never carry ____ where passengers sit.

options.text: Small arms ammunition
An oxygen tank
Radioactive materials
Drunk passengers

questions.correctAnswerText: Radioactive materials
questions.explanation: Buses cannot carry labeled radioactive materials in the passenger area.

questions.question: In general, a bus should be refueled:

options.text: With passengers on board.
With passengers on board only if it cannot be avoided.
With passengers on board if they agree.
By a passenger.

questions.correctAnswerText: With passengers on board only if it cannot be avoided.
questions.explanation: A bus should not be refueled with passengers on board unless absolutely necessary. Never refuel a bus with passengers inside an enclosed building.

questions.question: How can you prevent your vehicle from rolling backward when you start moving?

options.text: Slightly engage the clutch before lifting your foot off the brake pedal.
Put the vehicle in second gear.
Use the parking brake when you stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slightly engage the clutch before lifting your foot off the brake pedal.
questions.explanation: To stop your vehicle from rolling backward when you start moving after a stop, slightly engage the clutch before you lift your foot off the brake pedal.

questions.question: When inspecting a vehicle's springs, which of the following should you NOT do?

options.text: Look for missing leaf springs.
Look for broken coil springs.
Check that torsion springs are not damaged.
Glue cracked leaf springs.

questions.correctAnswerText: Glue cracked leaf springs.
questions.explanation: During a vehicle inspection, check for missing, shifted, cracked, or broken leaf springs. Also check for broken or bent coil springs and damaged torsion bars or torque arms. Never glue cracked leaf springs.

questions.question: How should carry-on luggage be stored?

options.text: In the aisle.
On the passengers' laps.
Near the doorway.
Secured so the driver can move freely and passengers can exit safely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Secured so the driver can move freely and passengers can exit safely.
questions.explanation: All luggage on a bus must be stored so the driver can move freely, passengers can exit through any door or window in an emergency, and items cannot fall and injure riders.

questions.question: What is the standee line?

options.text: A line on the floor of a bus that passengers cannot cross.
A single-file line of standing passengers.
A mark showing the maximum number of people allowed on a bus.
A mark showing the maximum height passengers can be.

questions.correctAnswerText: A line on the floor of a bus that passengers cannot cross.
questions.explanation: While a bus is moving, passengers cannot stand forward of the driver's seat. A two-inch line on the floor marks this boundary. This is called the standee line.

questions.question: What happens when driving in extremely hot weather?

options.text: You should not drive.
You need to remove oil from the engine.
It is safer with less coolant.
Tire pressure can increase.

questions.correctAnswerText: Tire pressure can increase.
questions.explanation: In extreme heat, tire pressure increases because air expands. Keep enough oil and coolant in your engine to prevent overheating.

questions.question: What can happen if the exhaust system is broken?

options.text: Poisonous fumes may enter the cab.
Poisonous fumes may exit the back of the muffler.
It may cause steering problems.
It may cause problems if the trailer is full.

questions.correctAnswerText: Poisonous fumes may enter the cab.
questions.explanation: A broken exhaust system allows poisonous fumes to enter the cab or sleeper. Check your exhaust system regularly for damage.

questions.question: What should you do at a railroad crossing during the driving test?

options.text: Pass another vehicle on the tracks if it is moving slowly.
Change lanes while on the tracks.
Do not change gears while on the tracks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not change gears while on the tracks.
questions.explanation: During the driving test, do not stop, change gears, pass another vehicle, or change lanes while any part of your vehicle is on the railroad tracks.

questions.question: What should you do before starting a vehicle inspection?

options.text: The inspection report is not important.
Review the report only if there will be passengers.
Review the previous inspection report if one exists.

questions.correctAnswerText: Review the previous inspection report if one exists.
questions.explanation: Always review the last vehicle inspection report first. Only sign the report if all noted defects have been repaired.

questions.question: When you approach your vehicle, what should you check?

options.text: That the vehicle looks shiny.
That it is not parked too close to other vehicles.
That there are no puddles under it that show a leak.
That it is parked properly.

questions.correctAnswerText: That there are no puddles under it that show a leak.
questions.explanation: When you approach your vehicle, check its general condition and look for damage or leaning. Look under the vehicle for fresh leaks. Also check around the vehicle for hazards like people, other vehicles, or low-hanging wires or branches.

questions.question: What should you do if you must drive through flowing water or a large puddle?

options.text: Speed up.
Gently apply the brakes.
Try to stop in the water.

questions.correctAnswerText: Gently apply the brakes.
questions.explanation: Avoid driving through large puddles or moving water if possible. If you must drive through water, slow down, shift to a low gear, and gently apply the brakes. This keeps water and mud out of the brake system.
